npcs.name: Captain Thorne Ironhelm
npcs.appearance: A grizzled man in dented plate armor stands behind a wooden desk.
npcs.greeting: Well met. If you're seeking work, you've come at the right time. Dark times are falling on Millhaven.

keywords.quest: The roads are unsafe. Caravans vanish, and young Elara Whitmore was taken three days ago.
keywords.elara: Sweet child. Disappeared from her farm. Her mother Marta is beside herself. Fifty gold if you find her.
keywords.creatures: Farmers speak of shadows moving. Animals found dead, or worse... corrupted. Brother Aldus believes it's dark magic.

barks.line: Millhaven owes you. Sit down before you fall down.
You are wet to the knee. Where have you been?
Anything?

npcs.name: Queen Liora
npcs.appearance: A strikingly beautiful woman in royal silks with a perfectly practiced, cold smile.
npcs.greeting: Ah, the heroes of Millhaven. How quaint. Perhaps you might join us for wine?

keywords.king: The King is adjusting to recent pressures. His paranoia is tiresome, but I remain steadfast.
keywords.covenant: Ah, you know. How delightful. We are not murderers, we are gravediggers for a dead world.
keywords.corruption: Such an ugly word. I call it 'transformation.' The shadow will purge the weak.

barks.line: Back from the library so soon? How diligent.
Again? The court will talk.

npcs.name: Malachai Vex
npcs.appearance: A tall, aristocratic man radiating magnetic charisma and faint, unsettling shadow.
npcs.greeting: At last we meet. Sit with me. Let us discuss the world as it truly is.

keywords.vision: The old order is a fossil. We will be perfected through the shadow.
keywords.shadow: Shadow is entropy—the natural force of ending. It grants clarity and power.
keywords.ascension: I am a Vessel. Soon, I will be consumed, and the true god will wear this flesh.

npcs.name: Marta Whitmore
npcs.appearance: A farm woman in a coat buttoned wrong stands at the fence, watching the treeline as if it might hand something back.
npcs.greeting: Are you from the Captain? Have you— no. No, you'd have said.

keywords.elara: She's nine. She's got my mother's temper and her father's ears, and she has never once in her life come home when she was called.
keywords.grove: The oak ring, back of the barn. Every child in the valley plays there, and every mother tells them not to.
keywords.doll: She takes it everywhere. She'd have had it with her.

barks.line: Elara! Look who has come.
What is that you are carrying? Let me see.
Any news? No. You would have said.

npcs.name: Brother Aldus
npcs.appearance: A priest in a plain grey habit kneels at the altar, sorting the week's offerings into what can be eaten and what cannot.
npcs.greeting: Ashkyr keep you. If you've come to leave something, there is room on the step.

keywords.burials: Four this week. Each of them dead longer than they'd been missing, and each of them came to me with their eyes full of earth.
keywords.shoe: Elara Whitmore's. Her mother brought it in. I keep meaning to give it back, and I can't decide whether that would be a kindness.
keywords.ashkyr: Ashkyr keeps the hearth and the grave. Lately the grave has been keeping me.

barks.line: Ashkyr keep you. I mean it rather more than usual.
Back again? The bread is fresh, if you want it.

npcs.name: Ada Harrow
npcs.appearance: The smith, broad and soot-grey, rests her hammer on the anvil and watches you the way she'd watch a horse she hadn't been told about.
npcs.greeting: If you want a horse shod, it'll be a week. If you want anything else, it'll be longer.

keywords.nails: People buy nails. I sell them.
keywords.commissions: Four this week I'll not be paid for. I stack them in the order I heard.
keywords.maul: Seal-stone in the head, off the old boundary marker. I made three and finished one.

barks.line: Hammer is quieter these days. Good.
Still here, then.

npcs.name: Wendel Pike
npcs.appearance: The landlord, a round and pleasant man with a cloth over his shoulder, has a habit of standing near whoever is talking.
npcs.greeting: Welcome to the Sparrow! Sit anywhere but by the door — there's a draught.

keywords.ale: Best in the valley, and the only one in the valley, which helps.
keywords.news: Tollgate on the capital road's shut till the Captain says otherwise, so half the county's drinking my cellar dry waiting on it. Ill wind.
keywords.lamp: For the late ones. Nobody wants to break their neck on the back stair in the dark.

barks.line: Come to gloat? Go on, then. Everyone else has.
You. You came back up the Mere Road.
Back again! What will it be?

npcs.name: Master Archivist Oswin Hale
npcs.appearance: A thin man in ink-stained cuffs sits behind the catalogue desk, with the fixed, careful attention of someone who has not slept properly in a year.
npcs.greeting: Quietly, please. The library is open to all subjects of the Crown. Mostly.

keywords.catalogue: Every volume this library has ever held, in the order it came to us. Including the ones it no longer holds.
keywords.missing: Removed for conservation, by order of the Crown.
keywords.seals: Not here. Not in front of the shelves. Ask me properly.

barks.line: Quietly, please. Oh. It is you. Thank you.
Find her. Please.
You found the letter. I can see it on your faces.
Yes?

npcs.name: Jory Tallow
npcs.appearance: A pedlar's cart stands against the fountain with its shutters propped open on more stock than a market town can afford. Its owner leans on the wheel, reading the same broadsheet for what is clearly the fifth time.
npcs.greeting: Customers! Actual customers.

keywords.road: Tollgate's shut till the Captain says the roads are safe, and the roads are not safe, so here I sit.
keywords.nails: Plenty of call for iron nails in this town, and nobody will buy mine. Somebody local is selling them cheaper, and I'd dearly like to know who.
keywords.prices: Capital prices. But they're fair capital prices.

barks.line: The wagon is in! Come and look, come and look!
Back for more? I knew you had taste.

npcs.name: Sal Mercy
npcs.appearance: A mule stands in the road loaded higher than any mule should be, a bell on its bridle, and beside it a small woman as brown as a walnut, counting something on her fingers that she does not intend to tell you about.
npcs.greeting: Mercy's the name, and it's the only thing I give away.

keywords.mule: Her name is Patience. She has none.
keywords.road: I go where the roads go. Lately they go to graveyards.
keywords.prices: Dear. It all rides on one mule, and you're paying for her feet.

barks.line: You are on the board, you know. Everybody is reading it.
You again. Anyone would think you were following me.

npcs.name: Foreman Ruel Brask
npcs.appearance: A heavyset man in a foreman's leather apron sits on an upturned ore cart by the tally board, turning a brass token over and over in his fingers.
npcs.greeting: If you're from the Crown, the answer's still no. If you're not, mind the shaft.

keywords.shift: Nine went down on the last shift. None came up. I have their tokens out, and nobody to give them back to me.
keywords.tally: A token going down, the token back coming up. That board has been wrong for a month.
keywords.deep workings: Crown's men put a guard on the bottom. Then the guard stopped coming up and all.

barks.line: Board is clean. First time in a month.
Well? Anything down there?

npcs.name: King Aldric
npcs.appearance: A gaunt man in a nightshirt, with the crown of Valorheim in his lap, sits on the lowest step of the dais rather than the throne, as if he has not yet decided whether it is still his.
npcs.greeting: You will be the ones I owe my wits to. Sit, if you like. There is nobody left in this room to tell you not to.

keywords.queen: My wife went down into the plaza the night it opened, with a length of chain and nobody to carry her train. I have been married to her for twenty years. I do not think I have met her.
keywords.sundering: The plaza split along a line older than the city. The surveyors say the palace was built along it on purpose. I should like very much to know whose purpose.
keywords.patrol: The Third Patrol went down the rift after her the same night, eight good men. The post they were keeping came down into the dark after them. Nobody has come back up.

barks.line: You came back up. I had stopped expecting anyone to.
Eight good men. Thank you for bringing them home.
Anything from below?

npcs.name: Bren Cask
npcs.appearance: A broad woman in a caravan guard's quilted coat sits with her back to the wall and a greatsword propped against the bench, making one ale last as long as one ale can be made to last.
npcs.greeting: If you're selling, I'm skint. If you're hiring, sit down.

keywords.caravan: Three wagons out of Valorheim. Something came out of the trees at dusk, thin and grey and moving like puppets. I cut one in half and it kept coming. I'm the only one who walked in.
keywords.hire: I'm a guard without anything to guard. Twenty gold and I'll guard you.
keywords.sword: Took it off a man in the capital who said he'd pay me back. He didn't. I kept the sword. Fair trade.

barks.line: Hiring yet?

npcs.name: Tamsin Reed
npcs.appearance: An elf in mud-green leathers crouches by the treeline, a longbow across her knees, untangling a snare that has caught nothing but leaves.
npcs.greeting: Quietly. Not that there's anything left in there to scare.

keywords.deer: Gone. Not hunted out: gone. Everything in that wood with the sense to run from something has run.
keywords.snares: A month of empty snares. I've started setting them for whatever is eating the deer.
keywords.hire: Twenty-five gold, and you'll have an arrow wherever you need one.

barks.line: Still nothing in the snares. Still something in the wood.

npcs.name: Sister Wren
npcs.appearance: A young sister of Ashkyr in a plain grey habit is scrubbing the temple steps that do not need scrubbing, with the air of somebody who would rather be anywhere else doing anything useful.
npcs.greeting: Ashkyr keep you. Mind the wet step.

keywords.aldus: Brother Aldus hasn't slept properly since the Whitmore girl went missing. He sits up with the old books, the ones about seals.
keywords.healing: I can mend most things that bleed. Not the things that don't, I'm told, but I've not met one yet.
keywords.hire: Fifteen gold for the poor box, and I'll come and keep you standing.

barks.line: Ashkyr keep you. The step is dry, today.

npcs.name: Ilse Marrow
npcs.appearance: At a copying desk heaped with other people's books, a thin woman with ink to the wrists is writing a letter of complaint to somebody, by the look of her, for the fourth time.
npcs.greeting: If you want a book, ask the Keeper. If you want an argument, I'm free.

keywords.academy: They threw me out of the Academy for setting fire to a lecturer. In fairness, he asked what the spell did.
keywords.seals: Somebody has been borrowing the books on the old seals and bringing them back with pages cut out. I have told the Keeper. The Keeper has told me to mind my own copying.
keywords.hire: Sixty gold, and you'll have somebody along who has actually read what you're getting killed over.

barks.line: Back again? Good. I was running out of people to be right at.

npcs.name: Grum
npcs.appearance: A dwarf the width of a door sits on the spoil heap with a greataxe across his knees and a miner's token on a cord round his neck, glaring at the shaft as if it owes him money.
npcs.greeting: Shaft's shut. Foreman's orders. Foreman's wrong.

keywords.brother: Something down there broke my brother's pick in half. With my brother still holding it.
keywords.shaft: They shut the deep workings and put a guard on. Then the guard stopped coming up. Now they just shut it.
keywords.hire: Forty gold. I want to hit something that deserves it.

barks.line: Still shut.

npcs.name: Vey
npcs.appearance: A halfling in a coat with a great many pockets leans on the plaza fountain, watching purses the way other people watch pigeons.
npcs.greeting: Lost something? No? Give it a minute.

keywords.palace: The palace kitchens order twice the bread they used to. Twice. And nobody new has been seen going in.
keywords.locks: There's no lock in Valorheim I haven't opened. There's a few I've opened twice, to be sure.
keywords.hire: Fifty gold, and you'll have every door between here and the palace. Pockets too, if you're not fussy.

barks.line: Still got everything? Check.

npcs.name: Sergeant Ada Rook
npcs.appearance: A Watch sergeant with a ledger under one arm and scarred knuckles is counting straw-packed crates stacked against the back wall, very carefully.
npcs.greeting: Stores. If you're not Watch, you're paying.

keywords.crates: Alchemy. The Captain ordered it for the wood, then worked out what it would do to the wood.
keywords.watch: Twelve of us for a town and a wood. Nine, since the Whitmore girl.

barks.line: Stores are open. Mind the crates.

npcs.name: Quartermaster Odile Venn
npcs.appearance: Under a Crown awning by the fountain, a grey-haired quartermaster in a buttoned blue coat is chalking prices onto slates beside a trestle of oiled steel.
npcs.greeting: Crown surplus. Every piece stamped and every price fixed.

keywords.surplus: The Crown is short of coin and long on swords.
keywords.palace: The Queen orders nothing through my stores any more. Somebody else is keeping the palace in something now.

barks.line: Back for more Crown surplus? It is not getting any cheaper.
